title: Check yourself: tasks and the board

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a subtask and a dependency?
questions.explanation: A subtask is a piece of this task and closes with it. A dependency is a separate task that must finish first — and Constellation enforces it: a task with an open dependency cannot be moved to done.

answers.text: A subtask is part of this task; a dependency is a different task that must finish before this one can proceed
A subtask is assigned to someone else; a dependency is assigned to you
They are the same thing shown in two places
A dependency is a note for humans; a subtask is enforced by the system

questions.prompt: You try to move a task to Done and Constellation refuses. Which of these could explain it? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Open dependencies and attached blockers both gate completion, and on a project with the GitHub CI setting on, a linked pull request with failing checks does too. Priority and due dates never gate anything — priority is a sorting signal for humans, and a missing due date just means no reminders.

answers.text: It has a dependency that is not finished yet
It has an unresolved blocker attached
Its priority is set to CRITICAL
It has no due date

questions.prompt: Which of these belong in a task's description? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The description specifies the work: what is in scope, what is out, and the acceptance criteria that decide whether it is done. Status lives in the column, and the conversation belongs in comments so it stays attached to the work.

answers.text: What is in scope and what is explicitly out
Acceptance criteria — the checklist that decides it's finished
A running log of who said what about it
The current status of the work

questions.prompt: Which of these is a well-formed task title?
questions.explanation: A good title says what will be true when the task is finished. "Wiring harness" names a topic, not an outcome — you cannot tell whether it's done.

answers.text: Route and secure the main wiring harness through bay two
Wiring harness
URGENT!! harness stuff
Talk to Priya about the harness

questions.prompt: You log 3 hours against a task. What happens?
questions.explanation: Anything over two hours in one entry is queued for an officer to approve before the reward is granted. That gate is what keeps the XP economy believable — it is a process rule, not an accusation.

answers.text: It's recorded, and the reward is queued for an officer to approve
It's rejected — 3 hours exceeds the per-entry limit
XP is granted immediately with no review
It's recorded but never earns XP

questions.prompt: Typing @someone in a task comment sends them a Slack DM as well as an in-app notification.
questions.explanation: True. Mentions are parsed on save, matched to members, and delivered both in-app and by Slack DM. That is what makes the comment thread a real place to ask a question rather than a message in a bottle.

answers.text: True
False
